title: Avionics Self Test(subfinal) (50Q)
description: 50-question self test covering all avionics modules (ET-AV01 to ET-AV07), with question counts per module following the exam blueprint. Questions are drawn from the AVO All Exams 2024 file.

questions.question: As the cross-sectional area of a conductor increases, its resistance:
questions.explanation: Resistance R = ρL/A, so a larger cross-sectional area gives more paths for electrons and lowers resistance.

questions.question: Which sub-atomic particle carries no electric charge?
questions.explanation: Protons are positive, electrons negative, and neutrons are electrically neutral.

questions.question: The RC time constant is the time for a capacitor to charge to what percentage of the source voltage?
questions.explanation: After one time constant (τ = RC) a charging capacitor reaches about 63% of the source voltage; it discharges to about 37%.

questions.question: An ammeter must be connected:
options: A. In series with the circuit
B. In parallel with the load
questions.explanation: An ammeter has very low resistance and must carry the circuit current, so it is placed in series.

questions.question: Why is a transformer core made of laminations?
options: A. To decrease eddy current losses
questions.explanation: Thin insulated laminations break up the paths of circulating eddy currents in the core, reducing heating and power loss.

questions.question: A transformer has 1000 primary turns on a 250 V AC supply and must give a 400 V secondary. How many secondary turns are needed?
For an NPN transistor to conduct, its base-emitter junction must be:
questions.explanation: An NPN transistor turns on when the base-emitter junction is forward biased (base positive relative to emitter).

questions.question: In a bridge full-wave rectifier, if one diode opens, the output becomes:
options: B. A full-wave output with double amplitude
questions.explanation: With one diode open, one half-cycle path is lost, so only half of each AC cycle is rectified.

questions.question: Which amplifier class gives the highest linearity and lowest distortion?
questions.explanation: A Class A amplifier conducts for the full 360° of the input cycle, giving the best linearity but the lowest efficiency.

questions.question: An astable multivibrator has how many stable states?
questions.explanation: An astable multivibrator continuously switches between two quasi-stable states, so it has no stable state and works as a free-running oscillator.

questions.question: What is the 2's complement of the binary number 10101011?
questions.explanation: Invert the bits (01010100) to get the 1's complement, then add 1 to get 01010101.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a universal gate?
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR can each build any other gate; XOR and XNOR cannot.

questions.question: How many select lines does an 8-to-1 multiplexer require?
questions.explanation: 2^3 = 8, so three select lines are needed to choose one of eight inputs.

questions.question: Which type of analog-to-digital converter is the fastest?
questions.explanation: A flash ADC uses one comparator per level and converts in a single step, making it the fastest type.

questions.question: A nibble is equivalent to how many bits?
questions.explanation: A nibble is half a byte, i.e. 4 bits.

questions.question: Which CPU register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
questions.explanation: The program counter points to the next instruction; the stack pointer tracks the stack and the accumulator holds data for the ALU.

questions.question: CISC and RISC stand for:
options: A. Complex Instruction Set Computing and Reduced Instruction Set Computing
B. Complete Instruction Set Computing and Restricted Instruction Set Computing
C. Common Integrated System Code and Reduced Integrated System Code
questions.explanation: CISC uses a large, complex instruction set; RISC uses a small, simplified set of instructions.

questions.question: Which type of display does not emit its own light?
questions.explanation: An LCD works by polarizing crystals that modulate a backlight; CRTs and LEDs produce their own light.

questions.question: When removing an aircraft battery, which terminal is disconnected first?
options: C. Both at the same time
questions.explanation: Disconnecting the negative (ground) lead first avoids accidental short circuits to the airframe when working on the positive terminal.

questions.question: What is the method of restoring the residual magnetism of a DC generator field?
questions.explanation: Flashing the fields applies a brief external DC source to the field windings to re-establish residual magnetism so voltage can build up.

questions.question: In modern aircraft, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) is used:
options: C. Only during emergency power loss
questions.explanation: The RAT deploys only when normal AC power is lost, supplying emergency power for flight-critical loads.

questions.question: The use of a Variable Frequency Generator (VFG) eliminates the need for:
questions.explanation: A VFG's output frequency varies with engine speed, so no CSD is required to hold a constant generator speed.

questions.question: The output of a typical aircraft static inverter is:
questions.explanation: Aircraft inverters convert DC battery power to 115 V, 400 Hz AC for essential loads.

questions.question: When the control unit reduces electrical load to an acceptable level after a system overload, this is called:
questions.explanation: Load shedding automatically disconnects non-essential loads to protect the remaining power source.

questions.question: The transformer inside a Transformer Rectifier Unit (TRU) is:
questions.explanation: A TRU steps 115 V AC down to about 28 V AC before rectifying it to 28 V DC.

questions.question: The starting current of a series-wound DC motor, passing through both field and armature windings, produces:
questions.explanation: Because the field flux is proportional to armature current, the series motor produces very high torque at start.

questions.question: Which DC motor is preferred for constant-speed operation?
questions.explanation: A shunt motor's field current is constant, so its speed stays nearly constant under varying load.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an encoder in a servomotor system?
questions.explanation: An encoder gives position feedback; a tachogenerator is used for speed feedback.

questions.question: The explosive device that breaks the diaphragm and discharges a fire extinguisher bottle is called a:
questions.explanation: A squib (cartridge) is fired electrically to rupture the bottle's diaphragm and release the agent.

questions.question: Which electromechanical transducer gives a variable AC output voltage proportional to the angular displacement of its input shaft?
questions.explanation: A Rotary Variable Differential Transformer measures angular displacement; an LVDT measures linear displacement.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cause of a false alarm in a fire detection system?
questions.explanation: Moisture can cause leakage/short paths in detector loops and trigger false fire warnings.

questions.question: Mixing two frequencies in a non-linear device is called:
questions.explanation: Heterodyning produces sum and difference frequencies and is the basis of the superheterodyne receiver's mixer.

questions.question: What is the length of a half-wave dipole antenna for 100 MHz?
questions.explanation: λ = c/f = 3×10⁸ / 100×10⁶ = 3 m, so a half-wave dipole is λ/2 = 1.5 m.

questions.question: The VHF communication frequency range is:
questions.explanation: Aeronautical VHF voice communication operates from 118 to 137 MHz; HF is 2–29.999 MHz.

questions.question: Which ELT frequency is the digital distress signal designed for the Cospas-Sarsat system?
questions.explanation: 406 MHz beacons transmit a coded digital signal; 121.5 and 243 MHz are older analog frequencies.

questions.question: What is the length of an ARINC 429 data word?
questions.explanation: An ARINC 429 word is 32 bits long (label, SDI, data, SSM and parity).

questions.question: Data transmission in a fiber-optic cable relies on which property?
questions.explanation: Light is guided in the core because it is totally internally reflected at the core–cladding boundary.

questions.question: Which part of the ILS provides horizontal (lateral) guidance?
questions.explanation: The localizer gives left/right course guidance; the glide slope gives vertical guidance.

questions.question: The operating frequency range of the radio altimeter is:
questions.explanation: Radio altimeters operate around 4.3 GHz; 108–112 MHz is the localizer band and 9–12 GHz is weather radar.

questions.question: In the A350-type warning classification, which level describes an abnormal situation requiring crew awareness and corrective action?
questions.explanation: Level 2 covers abnormal situations needing awareness and corrective action; Level 3 is an emergency needing immediate reaction.

questions.question: Why is the main instrument panel sloped forward from the vertical?
questions.explanation: Tilting the panel toward the pilot lets the eye look more directly at the dials, reducing parallax reading errors.

questions.question: Absolute pressure of a fluid minus atmospheric pressure is called:
questions.explanation: Gage pressure is measured relative to atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: A thermocouple's output voltage is produced by:
options: A. A change in wire resistance
B. The temperature difference between the hot and cold junctions
C. Expansion of a bimetallic strip
questions.explanation: Two dissimilar metals joined at a hot junction generate an EMF proportional to the temperature difference from the cold junction.

questions.question: Which thermocouple pair is used to measure Exhaust Gas Temperature of a turbine engine?
questions.explanation: Chromel-alumel withstands the high temperatures of turbine exhaust gas.

questions.question: In a capacitance fuel quantity system, which capacitor parameter changes as the fuel level changes?
questions.explanation: Fuel and air have different dielectric constants, so the capacitance changes as the tank probe is covered by more fuel.

questions.question: An airspeed indicator works using:
questions.explanation: The indicator senses the difference between pitot (total) pressure and static pressure, i.e. dynamic pressure.

questions.question: An electric gyro horizon erection cut-out operates automatically when the bank angle exceeds approximately:
questions.explanation: Erection cut-out disables the erection system in turns beyond about 10° of bank to avoid false erection errors.

questions.question: How many accelerometers are used in an Inertial Reference System (IRS)?
questions.explanation: An IRS uses three accelerometers, one for each axis (north-south, east-west and vertical).

questions.question: What is the purpose of a yaw damper?
questions.explanation: The yaw damper uses the rudder to damp the coupled yaw-roll oscillation known as Dutch roll.

questions.question: The nose-down tendency of an aircraft at high Mach number is called:
questions.explanation: Mach tuck occurs as the centre of pressure moves aft at high Mach; Mach trim compensates for it.
